title: Password reset codes
pr_description: Adds a two-step password reset flow: request_password_reset() issues a 6-digit code (delivery handled by the caller, e.g. email), and reset_password() sets a new password when the code matches.

defects.description: Reset codes are generated with the non-cryptographic random module, whose Mersenne Twister output is predictable. Must use the secrets module like the rest of this file.
Codes are stored in a process-global dict with no expiry, despite RESET_CODE_TTL_MINUTES being defined. A code stays valid forever (until used or process restart).
A 6-digit code can be brute-forced in at most a million attempts and nothing limits attempts or invalidates the code after failures; the comparison is also not constant-time.

After a successful password reset, existing session tokens are not revoked. If the account was compromised (the very scenario resets exist for), the attacker's session keeps working after the victim resets. Added during label adjudication: found by a system under evaluation, confirmed genuine.

Reset codes live only in process memory: any restart or deploy invalidates outstanding codes, and multiple workers (each with their own dict) make the flow fail randomly behind a load balancer. Added during label adjudication.
